name: Satellite Circuit Interference
description: When many satellite circuits (transponders) are used in the same frequency band, the signal from one circuit may interfere with another circuit.
learning_objectives: Explain how multiple satellite circuits operating in the same frequency band cause signal interference.
Identify the operational challenges of frequency band sharing among transponders.
common_pitfalls: Assuming different transponders in the same frequency band never affect each other.

learning_objectives: Calculate the received carrier power using transmit power, antenna gains, wavelength, and distance.
Account for various system and atmospheric losses in the link budget equation.
common_pitfalls: Confusing transmitter and receiver losses or misapplying the wavelength and distance ratio.

name: Bent-Pipe Transponder Combined C/N Ratio
description: Hence, the combined C/N ratio of a bent-pipe transponder satellite link is given by the inverse sum formula.
learning_objectives: State the inverse sum formula for combined carrier-to-noise ratios.
Analyze the combined C/N ratio performance of a bent-pipe transponder satellite link.
common_pitfalls: Adding C/N ratios directly instead of using the inverse sum formula.

name: Output Back-Off (OBO)
description: Output Back-Off (OBO) is the amount by which the actual operating output power is kept below the saturation power of the amplifier.
learning_objectives: Define Output Back-Off in the context of amplifier operating power.
Calculate or describe the difference between actual operating output power and saturation power.
common_pitfalls: Confusing Output Back-Off with input power levels or maximum theoretical gain.

name: Free Space Transmission Loss
description: Free space transmission loss is the loss in signal power as the electromagnetic wave propagates through space without any physical medium.
learning_objectives: Define free space transmission loss for propagating electromagnetic waves.
Explain how signal power diminishes as waves travel through space without a physical medium.
common_pitfalls: Assuming free space transmission loss is caused by atmospheric absorption or physical obstacles.

name: Uplink Transmission
description: Information from the transmitting earth station is sent to the satellite through the uplink.
learning_objectives: Define the uplink as the communication path from an earth station to a satellite.
Identify the origin and destination of information transmitted via the uplink.
common_pitfalls: Confusing uplink transmission with downlink transmission from the satellite to the earth.

name: Geostationary Satellite C-Band Parameters
description: A geostationary satellite carries a C-band transponder which transmits 20 watts into an antenna with an on-axis gain of 30 dB.
learning_objectives: Identify the typical power and antenna gain specifications for a C-band geostationary satellite transponder.
Apply given transponder wattage and antenna gain values to basic power calculations.
common_pitfalls: Treating decibel antenna gain values as linear power ratios without proper conversion.
